data.narrative: Final module: the student shipped a production-grade Team Collaboration feature by choosing Option B and then survived the module's capstone CI lesson. They wrote the full permission-boundary matrix (15 tests, deny AND allow), a capstone end-to-end integration test, API/setup/ADR/rollback docs, and verified the ship checklist with live probes (6/6 docs spot-checks, secrets scan clean, search-index plan verified). In BREAK/FIX they discovered two environment-dependent assumptions in AI-era tests (carol@example.com existed only via manual local seeding; the interface-contract test sampled pre-existing teams) and proved the fix by recreating the database from scratch via migrations and running the full suite: 157 passed, 0 failed.

dimension_scores.observation: Decomposed the ship work into precise deliverables (test suite, docs, CI, integration test) with explicit acceptance criteria and then executed each part cleanly.
dimension_scores.evidence: test_module8_permissions.py (15 boundary tests), test_module8_integration.py (single continuous journey), docs/API.md + SETUP.md + ADRs.md + ROLLBACK.md.

dimension_scores.observation: Caught the module's planted failure before it hit CI by auditing environment assumptions, and verified every ship-checklist item with evidence rather than assertions.
dimension_scores.evidence: Found carol@example.com was not seeded by migrations and the interface-contract test required pre-existing teams; verified via a fresh migration-only DB run (157 green).

dimension_scores.observation: Zero wasted iterations - the two environment-dependence bugs were fixed on first pass each, and the integration test was adapted once to the M7 link-owner comment scoping.
dimension_scores.evidence: migrate.py DEV_USERS + test_interface_contract.py setup/teardown fixed on first attempt; full suite green on the next run.

dimension_scores.observation: Chose Option B (Production-Grade) and later recognized the CI failure as the specific cost of that decision - AI tests are written against observable state, so environment assumptions need an explicit check even at a high review bar.
dimension_scores.evidence: Root-caused the BREAK failure to 'carol existed only because I created her manually in Module 07' and the 3-team sampling dependency, then codified the create-or-migrate guard.

dimension_scores.observation: Shipped a tested, documented, CI-integrated feature with a rollback plan; full suite is environment-independent.
dimension_scores.evidence: 157 tests pass against a database created only by migrations; docs spot-checks 6/6; secrets scan clean; CI yml verified including the trigram search-plan gate.

strengths: Converted the module's BREAK lesson into a real fix: added carol to migrate.py DEV_USERS and rewrote the interface-contract test to create its own sample teams with teardown - then proved it by running the whole suite on a freshly-migrated database.
Produced a genuine ship package: permission matrix, capstone integration journey, API/SETUP/ADR/rollback docs, and a VERIFY checklist with live evidence for all seven items.
Internalized the meta-lesson precisely: 'AI writes tests that pass in the context they were generated in; making them context-independent is a review problem, not a prompting problem.'
data.recommendation: Add the environment-independence check ('does this test create everything it references, or is it seeded by migrations?') to the standard test review checklist for every future AI-generated test - it would have caught both BREAK failures before CI.
